title: 1.8 Applications and Models

icans: I can solve a right triangle.
I can use angles of elevation and depression to solve real-life problems.
I can use bearings to solve navigation problems.

vocab: find all of its __________ sides and angles
the angle from the _____________ down to the line of sight
a ____________ given as an acute angle from north or south, like N 35° E

blocks.sec: Part 2 · Notes and examples (fill in each note, then work the example)

notes: Solving a right triangle: the acute angles add to _______________; use trig ratios for the sides.

blocks.stem: Solve right triangle ABC with C = 90°, A = 34.2°, and b = 19.4.
A 110-foot ladder leans against a building at 72° with the ground. How high up the building does it reach?

notes: Angle of depression from the top equals the angle of _______________ from the bottom (alternate interior angles).

blocks.stem: From a 200-foot cliff, the angle of depression to a boat is 16°. How far is the boat from the base of the cliff?

notes: Bearings: start at north or south, then turn _______________ or west.

blocks.stem: A ship leaves port and sails 12 miles on a bearing of N 25° E. How far north and how far east is it?
A ramp rises 3 feet over a horizontal run of 20 feet. What angle does it make with the ground?
An isosceles triangle has legs 12 and base angles 30°. Find its altitude to the base and the base.
A kite string is 20 meters long and makes a 70° angle with the ground. How high is the kite?

tickets.stem: In right triangle ABC, C = 90° and A = 40°. Find B.
From 30 ft away, the angle of elevation to a tree top is 45°. How tall is the tree?
Is N 60° W more north or more west?
